NEW YORK, now the football center of the country, formally makes
its debut in the National Football League, whose championship games
throughout the Middle West are marked by the same intercity rivalry and
enthusiasm that features the annual bascball races in the two big leagues.
The National Football League in no way conflicts with college football.
which is one of the finest of all sports.

The object of the Nationa! League, which now has twenty-
two teams in twenty-one cities as far West as Kansas City, is to provide
spectacular entertainment for the rapidly growing number of football en-
thusiasts and to afford an opportunity for numerous worthy young men to
earn extra income which will enable them to gain a better start in their pro-
The New York Giants' management regards itself fortunate in the en-
gagement of Bob Folwell as coach of the fist league team to represent this
city. Folwell has been prominently identified with football for over twenty
ycars—first as star player and captain at the University of Pennsylvania and
Pennsylvania and the United States Naval Academy.
The veteran coach quickly set about to assemble one of the most re-
markable teams in the game's history. With seven former All-Americans in
its lineup the Giants promise to be a streng contender for the league cham-
pionship although all its opponents have been especially reinforced to meet
the new rival from New York.
Any one of the Giants' stars would "make" the average strong eleven.
But Coach Folwell has on the New York team some of the greatest stars of
all time—Jim Thorpe, famous Indian who is flashing old-time brilliancy:
"Century" Milstead, one of Yale's greatest tackles: Bob Nash, former All-
American at Rutgers who captains the Giants; Lynn Bomar, the best end
the South developed, who came here especially to help New York win its
first football championship: Arthur Caruey, a graduate of the local public
schools who captained the Navy eleven in 1923 and carned All-American
honors at guard the same season; Ed McGinley, who was All-American
tackle at Pennsylvania last season; Joe Alexander, whose center play at Syra-
cuse is still a model for players throughout the country and numerous other
stars like Jack McBride, whose three field goals won for Syracuse against
Coach Folwell has moulded all these players into a smooth running
machine after many practice drills at the Polo Grounds-a task that was made
easier because each player is keen to bring a championship team to New

National League championship games are some of the most thrilling I have ever
seen. Not only is each position expertly played but the entire progress of the en-
counter is marked by intense rivalry.
Last year Cleveland, with an unusually powerful and versatile team, won the
league title. The Giants should be a strong contender for the championship although
we anticipate exceptional opposition from each team.
